HEADLINE: US Tech Stocks Set to Slide as AI Rout Hits Global Peers

blog.headline: AI Stocks Are Not Being Rejected. They Are Being Repriced.
blog.angle: A selloff in global tech names signals the gap between AI adoption and AI monetization, forcing founders to see that market trust holds only when expectation is matched by earnings proof.

linkedin.headline: The uncomfortable part of the AI selloff is that the story still works — the math just doesn’t yet.
linkedin.angle: Investors are not abandoning AI; they are questioning how long companies can defend premium valuations before the return on capital becomes visible.

facebook.headline: AI optimism just ran into valuation discipline.
facebook.angle: Weakness in Korean chipmakers pulled pressure onto U.S. tech stocks, raising the founder question: when does a strong market narrative need hard earnings proof to keep its price?

instagram.headline: Hype Meets The Earnings Test
instagram.angle: The AI rout shows that attention can lift a category, but only proof of monetization protects the multiple.

threads.thread_hook: The AI selloff is not a technology problem. It is a timing problem.
threads.angle: The sequence reveals why markets can believe in long-term adoption while still punishing companies for delayed earnings, stretched valuations, and unclear returns.

stories.story_question: If the AI story is still strong, why are tech stocks sliding?
stories.angle: The tension between believing in the technology and trusting the valuation before monetization is proven.
